title: Member of Technical Staff
description: About Seamflow Every plane, medical device, lift, battery and building has to be tested, inspected and certified before it reaches the world. It's the invisible layer that keeps the physical economy safe, and it still runs on Word documents, PDFs, spreadsheets and email. Seamflow is the software layer for that industry. We build AI-powered workflows for certification bodies, notified bodies and inspection companies: scheduling and resource planning, technical review, conformity assessment, field inspection, and document intelligence over messy real-world files. Where we are: Live in production inside some of the largest enterprises in the industry $4.5M seed, 14x oversubscribed , co-led by Northzone and Initialized Capital, the funds behind Spotify, Klarna, Coinbase and Reddit. Angels include Charlie Songhurst and Mario Götze. Demand is outstripping what we can build. That's the reason this role exists. The team Most of our engineers were olympiad medallists in maths, physics or informatics before they were engineers. The team has come to us from Google, Amazon, X, Yandex, McKinsey and Bain, and from founding-engineer seats at startups that went on to multi-billion-dollar valuations. We hire against a very high bar, and this role exists to raise it further. The role A Product Engineer owns the surfaces people actually work in. A coordinator planning a month of inspections across a fleet of auditors. A reviewer signing off on a technical file. These are dense, stateful workflows where the interface carries real consequences, and where the person using it has done the job for twenty years and will know immediately if the software doesn't understand it. You own product surface end to end: the interface, the backend that supports it, and the data model underneath. Every customer runs the work differently, so there's no template to fall back on. You decide what the right thing to build is, build it, and are the one who hears about it when it's wrong. You'll ship to production in your first week. What we're looking for We care far more about raw engineering strength than about matching a list of technologies. If you're excellent, we'll hire you whether you've spent the last three years in Rust, Go, Python, TypeScript, C++ or something we haven't heard of. Our stack is learnable in a fortnight. Judgement, speed and standards are not. What we're actually screening for: You've built something hard and put it in front of real users. Not a prototype, not a course project. Something that ran, broke, and got fixed. You build genuinely good interfaces , and you can go as deep on the backend as the feature requires. You can hold a complicated workflow in your head and find the version of it that's simple enough to ship. Speed with taste. You ship fast, and you're opinionated about what not to build. You go to the source. You'll read the customer's actual documents, join the actual call, and look at hundreds of real outputs. Signals we like, none of them required: founder or ex-founder, founding team experience, early engineer at a startup with a serious engineering culture, EF / YC / Antler, early or stealth-stage startup, design sense you can defend, open source you genuinely maintain. This is probably not for you if You want a strict boundary between work and life. We run one of the most ambitious startup cultures in Europe: fast paced, extremely high ownership, and in person in Shoreditch. You want a well-defined ticket handed to you each morning. You want to specialise narrowly and stay in your lane. What you get Real equity, and compensation that reflects a high bar Genuine ownership of product surface area from day one, with the founders in the room Relocation support and visa sponsorship, handled properly Lunch and dinner covered, 24/7 gym access, and any tool that makes you faster A small team with high standards, high trust, and no politics If this sounds like your kind of problem, apply. A short note on the hardest thing you've built goes further with us than a polished CV. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

Identify the right mix of healthcare professionals and content creators for each campaign. Establish measurable targets across outreach volume, response rates, partnership approvals, content delivery, cost efficiency and campaign performance. Oversee the team’s day-to-day outreach, follow-ups, creator communication, fulfilment coordination and administrative workflows. Build clear processes and operating rhythms that allow the team to manage a high volume of influencer activity accurately and efficiently. 3. Build a Scalable Creator Acquisition Pipeline Source creators across three routes: direct outreach, the TikTok Shop affiliate marketplace, and the established creator network available through our TikTok consultant. Convert the consultant's network into signed, producing partnerships rather than a list. Sustain the current output of hundreds of pieces of creator content per month across the seeding program, while building a separate affiliate creator pipeline for TikTok Shop. Develop partnerships with a strong focus on micro- and mid-sized creators, while selectively pursuing larger influencers when commercially justified. Create tailored outreach strategies for a competitive market in which larger brands may offer significantly higher creator fees. 4. Build the TikTok Shop Affiliate Program Own the TikTok Shop affiliate program for 2 products under one brand, from creator recruitment through commission structure, sample logistics and GMV performance. Set and manage commission tiers, open collaborations, targeted invites and any performance-based arrangements; decide where flat-fee and where commission-only makes sense. Own affiliate GMV as a number you're accountable for, and the unit economics behind it: cost per acquired affiliate, sample cost per producing creator, blended commission rate. Identify and develop the small number of affiliates who will drive the majority of GMV, and build repeat and exclusive arrangements with them. Work with the TikTok Affiliate Creative Strategist on creative direction. They own research, concept and brief content; you own creator supply, terms, relationship and program performance. 5. Own Campaign Execution and Creator Relationships Oversee partnerships from initial outreach and qualification through contracting, product delivery, content production, payment and performance review. Ensure creators receive clear briefs, campaign expectations, timelines and feedback. Build strong, professional relationships that encourage creators to become long-term brand advocates rather than one-off partners. Maintain an active and engaged creator community through regular updates, challenges, educational content and brand communications. Own claims compliance in creator content across both brands. Maintain the do-say/don't-say guidance creators work from, and make sure it holds at volume across seeding, affiliate and organic. Ensure FTC material-connection disclosure and platform-specific policy compliance on every partnership. TikTok Shop enforces supplement claims differently from Meta; both need to be handled correctly. 6. Turn Creator Content into Growth Assets Secure usage rights and TikTok ad authorization (Spark Ad codes) at the point of partnership, not retroactively. Establish a clear process for reviewing, categorizing and distributing creator-generated content. Evaluate content based on brand alignment, creative quality, audience relevance and potential commercial use. Work with Paid Media, Creative and Marketplace to route creator content to its highest-value use: paid social, marketplace listings, email and brand channels. Translate both organic and paid media learnings back into creator briefs so creators can produce stronger, more testable content. Supply the brand social channels with a steady flow of approved, on-brand creator content. Publishing and community management on brand-owned accounts sit with a separate role. 7. Own Tools, Vendors and Operational Excellence Manage our external partners - the TikTok consultant and content agencies - including scope, output quality, cost and the decision on when capability should move in-house. Own the influencer marketing stack end to end. We currently run SARAL; assess whether it, Modash, Lefty or an alternative best serves discovery, outreach, relationship management and reporting at our volume. Partner with Supply and Operations teams to ensure product kits are shipped accurately and on time. Oversee creator invoicing and payment workflows, ensuring submissions are accurate, approved and processed promptly. Identify bottlenecks and introduce scalable workflows, automation and documentation where appropriate. 7. Measure and Improve Performance You'll be measured on four things: TikTok Shop affiliate GMV, cost per usable content asset, branded search and marketplace lift attributable to creator activity, and content throughput against quality standard. Everything else is diagnostic. You'll manage a defined creator and sampling budget across both programs, with authority to reallocate between seeding and affiliate based on returns. Define and monitor the KPIs required to evaluate the health and commercial impact of the influencer program. Track outreach volume, open and response rates, approval rates, creator acquisition costs, content delivery, engagement, reach, conversions and return on investment. Build clear weekly, monthly and quarterly reporting for the Growth team and company leadership. Analyze performance by creator profile, product, platform, partnership structure, outreach message and content format. Maintain a structured testing roadmap covering outreach messages, incentives, creator segments and content approaches. How You’ll Succeed You combine strategic thinking with a willingness to remain close to execution. You create clarity for your team, hold people accountable and help them improve. You build a predictable pipeline of relevant creators and commercially valuable content. You use data and experimentation to improve response rates, partnership quality and return on investment. You can recognize creators who offer strong value beyond follower count alone. You build effective partnerships across Creator Marketing, Paid Media, Creative, Supply, Email Marketing and E-commerce. You introduce structure without slowing down execution. You communicate clearly, act quickly and resolve problems before they affect campaigns. You remain resourceful in a competitive market where budgets and creator expectations may not always align. You care equally about relationship quality, operational accuracy and commercial outcomes. What You Bring Required 5+ years in influencer marketing, creator partnerships or creator affiliate marketing, including at least one program you owned end to end with commercial accountability. Operator experience running a TikTok Shop or comparable creator affiliate program, with GMV or revenue you were personally accountable for. DTC or e-commerce experience in health and wellness, beauty, or another regulated consumer category. Experience managing or mentoring team members, with evidence you raised their output rather than just reviewed it. Experience managing external agencies, consultants or vendors: setting scope, holding quality, deciding when to bring work in-house. Experience structuring and negotiating both flat-fee and performance-based partnerships. Strong analytical skills and a track record of using campaign data to change decisions, not just report them. Evidence of an AI or automation workflow you built or deployed that measurably increased throughput. Be ready to walk through what it does and what it saved. Strongly preferred Ownership of brand-owned organic social channels, not only creator programs. You understand how owned content and creator content compound. Working knowledge of FTC material-connection disclosure and platform claim policy in a regulated category. You know what a creator cannot say about a supplement, and why the answer differs on TikTok and Meta. Experience collaborating with Paid Media or Creative to repurpose creator content into performance advertising, including securing ad authorization at partnership time. Hands-on with an influencer marketing platform - SARAL, Modash, Lefty or equivalent. Experience running influencer or creator programs across multiple brands or product categories. title: Senior Product Lifecycle Manager
description: Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve. We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that. Here’s what this particular role covers. 🛠️ About our Program Management Team Wayve’s Program Management team turns complex technical goals into coordinated delivery. Working closely with engineering, product, safety and validation teams, we align priorities, manage dependencies and bring clarity to ambiguous challenges. We combine technical depth with cross-functional leadership to help teams move faster, more predictably and with purpose—focusing on meaningful outcomes rather than process for its own sake. As Senior Product Lifecycle Manager, you’ll connect Wayve’s product milestones to the detailed technical plans, system-level artefacts and readiness evidence needed to deliver them. You’ll lead complex, multi-team programmes from one milestone to the next, ensuring teams work from a shared, credible plan across our Level 2 and Level 4 products. 🧠 Your day-to-day Partner with engineering and product leads to translate product milestones into integrated cross-team schedules, priorities and delivery plans. Review technical progress, backlog health, dependencies and system-level evidence to determine whether programmes are ready to move forward. Identify technical risks and sequencing bottlenecks early, then drive the decisions and mitigation plans needed to protect delivery. Facilitate difficult conversations around scope, resources and competing priorities, helping teams reach clear and practical decisions. Adapt plans quickly as technical understanding, product priorities or delivery constraints change. Communicate programme status, schedule changes, risks and decisions clearly and proactively across technical teams and senior stakeholders. 🧩 What you’ll be working on: Owning and maintaining integrated lifecycle plans for complex Level 2 and Level 4 product milestones, creating a clear source of truth across teams. Managing cross-team dependencies and critical-path activities across engineering, product, safety, verification and validation. Managing system-level artefacts throughout the product lifecycle, ensuring the right information and evidence are available at each milestone. Establishing clear milestone-readiness criteria and using technical status, metrics and backlog data to support evidence-based delivery decisions. Aligning programme scope, sequencing and resource decisions with Wayve’s strategic and commercial priorities. Improving lifecycle-planning practices and tooling so teams can identify risk earlier, coordinate more effectively and deliver with greater predictability. 🙌 You should apply if: You have 5+ years of experience leading complex, multi-team technical or product programmes, with responsibility for planning, execution and delivery across several engineering teams. You bring a strong background in the automotive or autonomous-vehicle industry and understand the complexity of delivering integrated vehicle and software products. You have the technical depth to work closely with engineers, evaluate complex system architectures and challenge delivery plans constructively—not simply track execution. You think in systems, understanding how technical decisions, dependencies and changes in one area affect downstream teams and product outcomes. You’re decisive under uncertainty and can make sound prioritisation and trade-off recommendations with incomplete or evolving information. You have a strong track record of identifying delivery, technical and dependency risks early and driving them through to resolution. You use metrics, technical evidence and backlog health to assess readiness and guide programme decisions. You’re product-minded and outcome-focused, connecting delivery decisions to customer value and business impact rather than process completion alone. You can facilitate challenging stakeholder conversations, resolve conflicting technical priorities and create alignment without relying on formal authority. You communicate clearly in writing and in conversation, tailoring complex programme information for both technical and business audiences. You’re proficient with Jira, Confluence and modern backlog, planning and programme-management tools. Experience working in a safety-critical, regulated or complex multi-stakeholder environment would be valuable. A programme-management qualification such as PMP, CAPM or PRINCE2 would be a plus. 🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement. More about Wayve: 🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines. Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility. How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working: This is a full-time role based in our London office. Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives. 🔍 The Interview Process: Our process is clear and respectful of your time: Initial call / recruiter screen (30 minutes) Competency Interviews (HM Call; 60 minutes) Deep-dive technical interviews (Stakeholder Management, Delivery Use Case; 2 hours) Final interview : mission & values alignment (45 minutes). We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability. What’s in it for you (Location dependant): 💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually ✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs 📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth 🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more A quick, honest note before you apply. Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one. If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you. At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law. For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve DISCLAIMER: We will not ask about marriage or pregnancy, care responsibilities or disabilities in any of our job adverts or interviews. However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory. title: Lead / Principal Engineer - Full Stack
description: <h3><span style="font-size: 18pt;">A different kind of organisation</span></h3> <ul> <li>High trust, transparency, and autonomy</li> <li>Small teams, high ownership, flat structures</li> <li>Radical compensation transparency</li> <li>Sense of ownership in collective success</li> <li>Work with exceptional people who deeply care about their craft</li> </ul> <h3><span style="font-size: 18pt;">The role</span></h3> <p>As a Principal Consultant, you're often the first person a customer meets to brainstorm a business problem. You should be at home debating distributed systems with engineers and framing decisions with leadership. You'll frame the problem with customers, shape the approach with the team, provide technical direction, and stay hands-on through delivery. You will work in self-managing, experienced, small, and high-impact teams, solving hard problems. This is a consulting & tech delivery role  and while you will not have direct reports, you will regularly influence teams, mentor practitioners, manage stakeholders, and guide organisations through complex technology and business decisions.</p> <h3><span style="font-size: 18pt;">What the work looks like</span></h3> <p>We can't promise which problem you'll pick up, but the menu right now looks something like this:</p> <ul> <li>Redesign a ClickHouse schema so an ad buyer can query 85 billion rows in under two seconds, and discover that pre-exploding the rows 168x is actually the right answer.</li> <li>Keep a vehicle telemetry platform moving billions of messages a day without the Kafka consumers falling over.</li> <li>Build the engineering spine of a mobile wallet used by more than two billion people across four continents.</li> <li>Ship the data product behind peer-review submissions for one of the world's largest scientific publishers.</li> </ul> <p>The list changes every quarter. The pattern doesn't: data-heavy, distributed, and often sitting on top of something that already exists and isn't perfect.</p> <h3><span style="font-size: 18pt;">What you'll do</span></h3> <h4>Frame Problems & Propose Solutions</h4> <ul> <li>Help customers find the right problem before jumping to a solution.</li> <li>Facilitate discovery sessions, architecture reviews, and technical workshops.</li> <li>Translate business goals into a technology strategy and an execution plan.</li> </ul> <h4>Lead Through Technical Excellence</h4> <ul> <li>Stay hands-on; contribute directly to design, architecture, implementation, and review.</li> <li>Make pragmatic calls balancing business needs, engineering quality, and delivery timelines.</li> <li>Guide teams to build scalable, resilient, secure systems  and the practices that keep them that way.</li> </ul> <h4>Influence, Advise, and align</h4> <ul> <li>Act as a trusted advisor on technology and investment decisions; assessments, due diligence, advisory.</li> <li>Build trust and alignment across Sahaj and customer teams</li> <li>Converge competing priorities into a path forward.</li> <li>Communicate complex ideas clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.</li> <li>Shape new work through discovery and proposals; mentor others and raise the bar as you go.</li> </ul> <h4>Operate Across Technology Domains</h4> <p>Distributed systems, data engineering, AI & agentic systems, DevOps/SRE. Depth in few areas; breadth across, and appreciation for trade-offs in context.</p> <h3><span style="font-size: 18pt;">You'll thrive here if</span></h3> <ul> <li>You reach for the simplest solution that gets the job done and distrust accidental complexity.</li> <li>You think in systems, not isolated parts.</li> <li>You stay calm when the path is unclear and build clarity for those around you.</li> <li>You move easily between the org-level picture and the technical detail.</li> <li>You're curious by default and pick up new domains fast.</li> <li>You'd rather be in the room with a customer solving a real problem.</li> </ul> <h3><span style="font-size: 18pt;">What we're looking for</span></h3> <ul> <li>Demonstrable building software systems in complex environments.</li> <li>Strong engineering fundamentals; expert in at least one language, ideally polyglot.</li> <li>Hands-on experience designing and delivering distributed systems at scale.</li> <li>Deep grasp of architecture, system design, and engineering trade-offs.</li> <li>Direct experience working with customers and business stakeholders.</li> </ul> <h2><span style="font-size: 18pt;">What will you experience in terms of culture at Sahaj?</span></h2> <ul> <li>A culture of trust, respect and transparency</li> <li>Opportunity to collaborate with some of the finest minds in the industry</li> <li>Work across multiple domains</li> </ul> <h2><span style="font-size: 18pt;">What are the benefits of being at Sahaj?</span></h2> <ul> <li>Unlimited leaves</li> <li>Life insurance & private health insurance</li> <li>No hierarchy</li> <li>Open Salaries</li> </ul> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

description: <h2><strong>Pre-Sales Solution Consultant (People Analytics)</strong></h2> <h3><strong>Who We Are</strong></h3> <p>One Model is seeking a passionate <strong>Pre-Sales Solutions Consultant</strong> to help us scale our market presence in EMEA and bridge the gap between deep HR data capability, Workforce Intelligence, AI Measurement and Transformation,  and strategic business value.</p> <p>With customers and staff around the world, One Model offers a complete workforce intelligence platform along with a cutting-edge AI Impact evaluation tool.  Our products feature cloud-hosted data orchestration and advanced visualization and analytics tools all controllable via AI interfaces. Our platforms enable companies to unlock the real value of their HR and AI usage  data from the lens of the workforce.</p> <p><strong>This isn't your standard, script-reading sales demonstration role.</strong> We aren't looking for a "demo expert" who only knows which buttons to click, nor are we looking for someone with extensive People Analytics or HR experience.</p> <p><strong>The ideal fit:</strong> You are a proven pre-sales consultant who loves being a part of the sales process. You are able to quickly learn our products and basic people analytics concepts so that you can establish yourself as a knowledgeable trusted advisor in the sales process. </li> <li><strong>Gets it Done: </strong>You get it done, quickly and correctly.  You aren’t afraid to jump into the deep end and absorb as much as you can as fast as you can. You know each demonstration is an opportunity to grow and improve. </li> <li><strong>Not Afraid to Sell: </strong>You understand that this role is a critical part of the sales process and as such, you are able to build excitement about the One Model products and clearly explain its value proposition.</li> <li><strong>Natural Charisma & Presence:</strong> You are an exceptional communicator who commands a room or a web call. You genuinely enjoy meeting new people, building rapport quickly, and reading an audience to adjust your presentation style on the fly.</li> <li><strong>The Storyteller & Translator:</strong> You can develop a people analytics mindset, but your real superpower is translation. You can confidently discuss advanced analytics, metrics development, and system adoption with CHROs, HR leaders, AI Transformational Officers just as easily as you can discuss data logic with IT and Technical Buyers buyers.</li> <li><strong>Thrives in Momentum:</strong> You are adaptable, comfortable with a fast-paced scale-up environment, and can manage your time effectively when juggling multiple priorities.</li> <li><strong>What This Role Is NOT:</strong> This is a consultative, high customer-facing pre-sales role, NOT a backend data analytics or engineering position, nor is it a post-sales consulting role. This is not an applied People Analytics role, nor does it involve coding or data architecture work. </li> <li><strong>Location:</strong> We are a remote organization, supporting our employees to work from home. Ideally, you will be located near London, but we will consider candidates in the UK, followed by candidates in continental Europe. </li> </ul> <p><strong>Schedule: Hours of operations may vary depending on business needs. This role does provide some support for Account Executives located in the Eastern Time Zone in the US. As such, there will be situations where you will be expected to respond to Slack messages and support calls into the evening hours (London time). </strong></p> <h3><strong>Want to skip the line and guarantee your application gets reviewed?</strong></h3> <p>The "Show Us Your Spark" Video Challenge:</p> <p>While this video is optional, candidates who submit a video will be heavily prioritized and fast-tracked straight to the interview round. We are looking for people who can command a room, so this is your chance to stand out.</p> <p>We don't want a long, dry, feature-by-feature software demo. Instead, record a quick 2-to-3-minute video (using Loom, Zoom, or your phone) answering one of the prompts below:</p> <ul> <li>The 2-Minute Pitch. Pitch us your favorite app or tool on your phone right now. You have 2 minutes to make us want to download it immediately.</li> </ul> <p>The Golden Rule: Keep it under 3 minutes. If it feels like a dry, robotic corporate slide-read, you're doing it wrong! We aren’t grading your video editing or lighting; we are looking for your natural charisma, clarity, and ability to keep an audience engaged. Have fun with it.</p> <h4><strong>How to Submit Your Video:</strong></h4> <p>Please email your video file or link (Loom, YouTube, Drive, etc.) directly to ----- with the subject line: [Your Name] - Solutions Consultant Video Entry. Ensure your standard application is also submitted through our job board.</p> <h3><strong>We Support You As An Individual By</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Fostering a friendly, inclusive, respectful workplace culture.</li> <li>Supporting flexible work options, including 100% remote work and flexible hours.</li> <li>Coaching and development through our "Growing Together" conversations.</li> <li>Generous compensation, benefits, and professional mental health support (EAP).</li> </ul> <p><em>At One Model, we see the immense value of a diverse workforce. We encourage you to apply for the role even if you don't think you check every single box.</em></p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="title">Base Salary Range</div><div class="pay-range"><span>£100,000</span><span class="divider">—</span><span>£115,000 GBP</span></div></div></div> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Staff AI Engineer, Developer Productivity
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.</p> <p>Empowering the world starts with living <a href="https://ouraring.com/about-us">our values</a> and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office. </p></div><h2><strong>About the role</strong></h2> <p>Oura is rebuilding how it builds software. Every engineer has agentic tooling, and our own pipeline already takes a well-formed ticket to a reviewed, tested commit stack. It runs interactively, headless, and on a cloud sandbox fleet, with its own evals and tracing. We are looking for engineers who use AI as a fundamental building block of both the products we ship and the way we build them.</p> <p>That is a strong start on one stage of the lifecycle. The next step is the whole loop. As a Staff Engineer on the AI Transformation team, you will architect and own the system that turns agentic development from something power users do into the way hundreds of engineers across iOS, Android, backend and AI services ship every day. That means spec and intake, planning, implementation, review, testing, CI/CD, release, observability and incident follow-up, each with agents doing real work and humans keeping judgment where it matters.</p> <p>This is a fast-moving, LLM-forward team. We prioritize rapid prototyping, iterative loops and AI-native development, with the speed of a startup and the reach of a product used by millions of members. You can work hybrid from our UK office in London. You will need the existing right to work in the UK; we are not able to sponsor a visa for this role. </p> <p>You will build the pipeline, measure it, and make it trustworthy enough that teams choose it. Success is measured in validated changes reaching members faster and safer: time to a trustworthy signal, escaped defects, cost per merged change, and how many squads run on the paved path because it is better, not because they were told to.</p> <h2><strong>What you will do</strong></h2> <p>You don't need to do all of these on day one, but these are the kinds of problems you'll own:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Set the technical direction for the agentic pipeline:</strong> Make our existing ticket-to-PR pipeline dependable infrastructure. Own its architecture, including agent orchestration, context management and tool calling, and improve its reliability, throughput, cost and developer experience across mobile, backend and web repositories. title: Senior Talent Acquisition Partner, Engineering
description: About Us Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar. Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes. 2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR , with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler. We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law. Joining Legora means three things. We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions. We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback. We grow together: as a team and with our customers. Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts. If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place. The Role Legora has grown from 40 to more than 900 people in 18 months. During that time, we reached $100M ARR, tripled our valuation in five months, and continued expanding into new markets around the world. Our Talent Acquisition function is now entering its next chapter. The processes, standards, and hiring approach that support our next phase of growth are being built today, which you’ll play a significant part in. You'll work closely with senior leaders from day one and play a key role in shaping how Legora hires and scales. What you’ll do Product velocity depends on having the right engineering and technical talent in place, fast, and at a high bar. As a Talent Partner, you will own that directly. You are not a support function for the Engineering team. You bring genuine craft to how technical hiring gets done, and you're accountable for the quality and pace of the people who build Legora's product. You will own end-to-end hiring across engineering in UK&I, working closely with senior leaders who are genuinely invested in recruiting, trusted to make high-impact decisions on hiring and team composition. Specifically, you will: Own full-cycle recruitment across UK&I, partnering closely with hiring managers to define role scope, success profiles, and hiring strategies aligned to business priorities. Help shape how Talent operates at Legora, contributing beyond hiring to process design, programs, tooling, and broader People initiatives. Build and nurture proactive talent pipelines for critical and future hiring needs, ensuring we stay ahead of demand rather than reacting to it. Run structured, data-informed hiring processes that balance quality, pace, and consistency while maintaining a high bar for talent. title: Commercial Director
description: Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction . Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people , making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone. THE TEAM • ~160 people , around half in engineering, product and data • 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research • Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle • An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking , tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation The Opportunity This is one of the highest-leverage commercial roles in the business. As Commercial Director, you'll own the entire sales system at Relay — strategy, structure, process, and performance across all four of our segments: Pitstop/Field Sales, Enterprise, Large Parcel, and SME Parcel. If you want to shape how a fast-growing carrier goes to market at scale — and leave a lasting mark on how that machine works — this is the role. What You'll Own Sales strategy and structure Design the shape of Relay's sales organisation across all four segments — how they relate, where they overlap, how resource is prioritised Define the sales motion for each segment: who it sells to, how, and through which channel Keep strategy current as the business and market evolve Data and performance management Set the metrics that matter across pipeline, conversion, quota attainment, and productivity Build or oversee the dashboards that surface them Use data to make decisions on resourcing, territory design, and where to invest or pull back — instinct complements data here, it doesn't replace it Process, structure, and scalability Own the sales playbook, forecasting cadence, deal review process, CRM hygiene standards, and comp and quota-setting principles Upskill and coach the existing team on pitch, process, and performance Build infrastructure that scales for the next three years, not just today's headcount Team leadership and org design Lead the four segment sales leads (Pitstop/Field, Enterprise, Large Parcel, SME Parcel) and any central sales ops or enablement partners Decide what's centralised across functions versus what each segment lead owns locally Hire, develop, and coach those leads so each can build out their patch well Global and remote team leadership Lead teams remotely across time zones and geographies as Relay expands into the Americas and Europe Proven capability to do this is a requirement — it can't be learned on the job here Exec partnership and GTM planning Partner with the CCO and other function leads on revenue planning, headcount decisions, and commercial trade-offs Translate company strategy into a sequenced sales roadmap and GTM direction Push back clearly when targets or timelines aren't realistic Who Will Thrive in This Role Multi-motion sales leader. You've led more than one kind of sales motion — for example, high-volume SMB or transactional sales alongside enterprise or mid-market relationship-led sales. You're comfortable setting standards and managing performance across both. You've carried a number yourself and led others doing the same. This isn't a role for a single-lane specialist. Data-driven and structured operator. You define the metrics that matter, build or oversee the dashboards, and use data to make resourcing and process calls — not gut feel alone. You have a track record of introducing or significantly upgrading forecasting discipline, CRM hygiene, territory design, and comp structures in ways that improved consistency and scalability. You think in systems across a multi-year horizon, not just the next quarter. Global and remote team builder. You've led sales teams across multiple geographies or time zones, ideally including the US and Europe. You're comfortable setting standards, culture, and expectations remotely. Having helped take a company into a new country is a bonus; the core requirement is proven capability. People leader and org designer. You've led sales managers or leaders — not just individual contributors — and operated at least one layer removed from the front line. You have a track record of hiring and developing leaders beneath you, and making clear calls about what to centralise versus what to delegate. Exec partner. You've partnered directly with a CEO, founder, or C-suite on revenue planning and commercial trade-offs. You can push back on unrealistic targets while maintaining trust, and you can translate company strategy into an actionable, sequenced sales roadmap. Builder, not just operator. You've introduced new process, data infrastructure, or org structure in a previous role — not only operated within a system someone else built. This role is not about being a super-IC closer or a sector-pedigree hire; logistics experience is welcome but not a requirement or a filter. Compensation, Benefits & Workplace Generous equity, richer than 99% of European startups, with annual top-ups to share Relay’s success. Private health & dental coverage, so comprehensive you’d need to be a partner at a Magic Circle law firm to match it. 25 days of holidays Enhanced parental leave. Hardware of your choice. Extensive perks (gym subsidies, cycle-to-work, Friday office lunch, covered Uber home and dinner for late nights, and more). Who Thrives at Relay? Aim with Precision: You define problems clearly and measure your impact meticulously. Play to Win: You chase bold bets, tackle the hard stuff, and view constraints as fuel, not friction. 1% Better Every Day : You believe that small, consistent improvements lead to exponential growth. You move quickly, deliver results, and learn from every experience. All In, All the Time : You show up and step up. You take ownership from start to finish and do what it takes to deliver when it counts. People-Powered Greatness : You invest in your teammates. You give and receive feedback with care and candour. You build trust through high standards and shared success. Grow the Whole Pie : You seek out win-win solutions for merchants, couriers, and our customers, because when they thrive, so do we. If these resonate, and you combine strong technical fundamentals with entrepreneurial drive, let’s connect. title: Mid-Level Software Engineer
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>At Ledgy, we’re on a mission to make Europe a powerhouse of entrepreneurship by building a modern, tech-driven equity management and financial reporting platform for private and public companies. In 2026, we aim to be the leading provider for European IPOs and reporting for share-based payments. We are a value-based company with a core focus on being humble, transparent, ambitious and impactful, all in order to delivery the best experience for our customers and end users.</p> <p>We are proud to partner with some of the world’s leading investors. New Enterprise Associates led our <a href="https://techcrunch.com/2022/09/21/ledgy-a-carta-for-european-startups-to-manage-equity-and-cap-tables-raises-22m-from-nea-sequoia-and-more/">$22m Series B</a> round in 2022, with Philip Chopin joining Sequoia’s Luciana Lixandru on our board.</p> <p>We were founded in Switzerland in 2017 and today we operate globally from offices in Zurich and London. We encourage diversity and are an international team coming from 26 different countries and speaking 25 different languages.</p> <p> </p></div><p><strong>About the role</strong></p> <p>As a <strong>Mid-level Software Engineer</strong> at Ledgy, you’ll build reliable, scalable product experiences that help companies manage their equity with confidence. You’ll work closely with experienced engineers, product managers, and designers to turn complex equity workflows into clear, automated, user-friendly software.</p> <p>This role is a strong fit if you’re ready to take ownership of well-scoped projects, grow your technical judgement, and contribute across the stack while learning from senior peers.</p> <p>Location: We hire remotely across the UK, Spain, Germany, Poland, and Romania. For candidates based in London, we use a hybrid model with 2 days in the office per week.</p> <p><strong>Teams we are hiring for:</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Core Equity</strong> — Owns the foundational logic that powers Ledgy’s equity engine. Every equity-related event — such as issuing shares, creating new pools, or adjusting ownership — generates transactions. This team defines and maintains the transaction logic, data model, and core domain behaviour that ensure Ledgy’s platform remains accurate, scalable, and compliant. They also enable employees to sell their shares seamlessly once vested.</li> <li><strong>Workflows & Automation</strong> — Focuses on automating complex equity workflows and integrating with third-party services, including the trading exchange. The team builds systems that help company admins efficiently onboard and offboard employees, automate equity grants and terminations.</li> <li><strong>Reporting</strong> — Transforms Ledgy’s core equity data into financial, operational, and compliance reports. The team manages large, complex datasets and ensures reporting is accurate, performant, and reliable across jurisdictions and company structures. Their work powers the insights companies and auditors rely on for decision-making and transparency.</li> <li><strong>Tax</strong> — Ensures taxes are correctly reflected throughout equity operations, especially moments such as exercising, selling, mobility, and other taxable events. As a future team, Tax will build end-to-end product capabilities across the stack, helping customers manage complex tax and compliance requirements accurately across jurisdictions.</li> </ul> title: (Senior) Account Executive - Future Opportunities
description: <p>Weekly office requirement: Mon/Tues/Thurs weekly</p> <p>At GWI, we’re always looking for extraordinary people who thrive on making an impact. Those values are what got us where we are today, and they’re a big part of what we look for in our people.<br>While we’re not actively hiring for this role right now, we’re keen to connect with Senior Account Executives for future opportunities at GWI. If you’re interested in working with us but haven’t quite spotted the perfect role yet, we’d love you to join our proactive talent community. You’ll need to be flexible, comfortable with continuous change, and working in a high-tempo environment.</p> <h2>What do I need to bring with me? 🧳</h2> <p><br>You’ll need to be able to demonstrate the core skills this role requires. You don't have to tick all the boxes right away; the important thing is that you’re willing to learn. Here’s what the team will be looking for in you:<br>👉 Experience in SaaS or Subscription/licensing sales, especially closing business in large and complex corporate accounts.<br>👉 Ability to apply strategic thinking and sales skills to align technology solutions with complex, multi-stakeholder business problems.<br>👉 Follow MEDD(P)ICC sales methodology to qualify opportunities and progress deals through the pipeline.<br>👉  Experience using Salesforce to manage business (sales-cycle, pipeline,<br>forecasting, etc.).<br>👉  Excellent communication skills with the ability to communicate complex ideas<br>clearly and succinctly<br>👉  You are a hunter who sees the value of outbound prospecting to grow your own<br>sales pipeline, in addition to inbound leads<br>👉  Ability to reach and develop relationships with C-level executives<br>👉 Have experience working in a start/scale-up environment</p> <p>Equally important is attitude. We want people who think big (to make an impact), ask why (to find a better way), and show respect (to everyone, at every level, all the time). Those are our values, and they’re a big part of what we’re looking for in you.</p> <h2><strong>Our benefits</strong></h2> <p>Great benefits make a big difference. Not just to employees, but to the whole vibe of a business. That’s why when you work for us, you’ll enjoy a full spectrum of generous perks, rewards and office benefits.</p> <ul> <li>Competitve annual leave (excluding bank holidays) and December holiday office closure days on top</li> <li>Flexitime</li> <li>Early finishes on Fridays (4:30pm weekly, and 1pm during summer)</li> <li>Work from Anywhere in the world - up to 15 days</li> <li>Hybrid home/office working</li> <li>Latest tech equipment + WFH office budget</li> <li>A genuine commitment to mental and physical health, with a range of content, tools, and perks to help you look after your wellbeing</li> <li>OneGWI - the team that focuses on D&I in the workplace</li> <li>And more!</li> </ul> <h1><strong>Who we are</strong></h1> <p>GWI was founded with the knowledge that understanding your audience is really important for business. When you know who you’re speaking to and why, you can create content and campaigns that stand out to the people that matter.</p> <p>Through our global online survey, we gather data on the behaviour and perceptions of consumers across the world. This provides businesses with deep, actionable insights on their audience, revealed from data they trust.</p> <p>It’s been going well, too. Since launching in 2009, we’ve become one of the UK’s fastest growing target audience companies. We’re not about to stop growing any time soon. As a business, we’re on a mission to re-engineer data-driven marketing, and we’re on the lookout for talented people to join us.</p> <h2><strong>Diversity & Inclusion</strong></h2> <p>Imagine if our data came from just one kind of person. We’d get a very nuanced view of the world. And we definitely wouldn’t have got off the ground as a business.</p> <p>Although things certainly aren’t perfect, we live in a society where differences are increasingly celebrated – so we’d expect nothing else from our teams.  In fact, the GWI office is as diverse as our global data, it’s really important to us that it stays that way.  This is a place to feel at home, express yourself freely and make your mark.</p> <p><iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/2g0akAyAlUU" width="560" height="314"></iframe></p> <p>#LI-DNI</p> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

The product V7 Go helps teams turn complex, repeatable work into AI workflows they can run, review and improve . title: Senior People Partner - Content
description: About 9fin 9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets — the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion. Debt markets are vast, global, and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs, and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this broken infrastructure with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis, and high-value workflows across global markets. Today, 9fin powers teams at 300+ blue-chip institutions worldwide, including global banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms, and advisors. The business is scaling at exceptional speed, with rapid expansion in the US and best-in-class retention driven by deep workflow adoption. We’re at a defining inflection point. With proven product-market fit and strong, global market pull, 9fin is accelerating toward becoming the category-defining platform for debt markets worldwide. The opportunity Our People Partners are the eyes and ears of the organisation, embedded within their functional areas to be a sounding board for leaders, support managers and enable teams to thrive. The People Partnering team operate on a strategic and tactical level, ensuring the people elements are in place for teams to effectively deliver their strategic objectives (think org design, upskilling, succession planning) whilst also offering one on one support, both structured and ad hoc, to those who need it most. We're hiring an experienced, driven Senior People Partner to partner with our Chief Content Officer and the Content (Editorial, Legals, Credit, Distressed) team. Content is scaling fast across the UK and US, and we need a Senior People Partner who can move at pace, get to grips with what the team actually does, and hold their own with senior editorial and analytical leaders. You'll be fully embedded in the Content team, with a real voice in leadership meetings, editorial rituals and off-sites. You'll know the leads, managers and rising talent well enough to catch the people issues long before they show up in engagement scores or exit interviews. Every day is different, but here's an example of the kind of things you'll work on: Strategic Trusted advisor to your leaders : You'll be the first person Content leadership calls on anything people-related: the confidant, sounding board and thought partner they think alongside, not the person they update after the fact. That kind of trust is earned over time, through showing up and being willing to have the harder conversation when it matters. Right hand person to the CCO: You know how he thinks about content and his organisation, and are confident acting as his proxy with his leaders to get them to where they need to be. Locked in on what the team is trying to achieve : You know Content's goals, what its leaders and teams do. You bring solutions, not just observations, and follow them through to completion. Fully embedded in your team : You're in the rituals, Slack channels and meetings that matter, so you've got a real read on how the team actually works. You cut through the noise to name the actual issue and get it resolved quickly and respectfully. Catching things early : You join the dots across 1:1s, skips, engagement data and your own observations to surface people risks while they're still small and easy to fix. You coach leaders and managers to build the same instinct. Org design : You advise on org shape, spot gaps and flag future risk areas. You make sure the right people are doing the right jobs at the right level as Content scales across regions and coverage. Talent management : You know who the key talent is and you work with leaders to develop, stretch and reward them. You support leaders to identify their successors and build the development plans that get them ready. You work proactively with the Talent team on the pipelines for roles you can already see coming. Learning & development : You spot where Content teams need to grow — editorial craft, analytical rigour, management skill, leadership development — and you lead the training that plugs the gap. A big part of that is upskilling managers to handle people issues themselves, early and well, rather than escalating them to the CCO. You diagnose early, source or build the right thing, and hold a bar for what impact should look like once it's landed. Reward : You use solid data to inform our salary bands and keep compensation fair across the team, with D&I front of mind. You coach leaders and managers through promotion and salary reviews so decisions are thoughtful, equitable and defensible. Performance : You help leaders and managers get the best out of their teams, surfacing blockers, coaching through them, and making sure feedback and training actually land. You hold a high bar yourself and help leaders hold one too. Hands up for the bigger stuff : You take on projects that improve the People function as a whole, not just your patch. You scope them properly, influence stakeholders, manage the risks and dependencies, and ship on time. Tactical Employee Relations (ER) : Following UK employment law, navigating all employee relations within your business area, including but not limited to: managing Performance Improvement Plans (PIPs), resolving claims and grievances in line with policy, probation management, maternity and paternity cases, flexible working requests, conflict management and mediation, and any other employee-to-employee issue that comes up, both formally and informally. Embedding people products : Working with the wider Partnering team to embed our people products and systems, delivering training, championing adoption and being the go-to person for questions. Delivering product feedback to the wider team on a regular basis. Data : Pulling and analysing the right data to help managers and leaders make good calls and adding the context that turns numbers into something your leaders can actually use. Wellbeing support : 1:1 support to employees when they need it, and making sure they know what mental and physical health support is on offer. Supporting managers through those conversations too. description: <div class="content-intro"><h2>Who <strong>We Are</strong></h2> <p>Lightning AI is the company behind PyTorch Lightning. You will design systems that enable engineers and software to interact programmatically with thousands of servers, storage systems, and high-performance networks, reducing manual operations and making infrastructure management more reliable, repeatable, and scalable.</p> <p>This is a software-first infrastructure role that combines strong software engineering with Linux systems and hardware-aware infrastructure automation. You will work closely with teams across Infrastructure, Networking, Data Center Operations, and Platform Engineering to bring new capacity online and continuously improve how we operate our infrastructure at scale.</p> <p><em>This role may be fully remote within the U.S., or hybrid out of one of our office hubs (NYC, SF, Seattle, or London), with occasional team and company offsites. We are not able to provide visa sponsorship for this position at this time.</em></p> <h2><strong>What You Will Do</strong></h2> <h3><strong>Infrastructure Software & Automation</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Design, build, and operate production services, APIs, tooling, and automation for managing large-scale bare-metal and GPU infrastructure</li> <li>Build and extend software systems that support infrastructure provisioning, configuration, monitoring, and lifecycle management</li> <li>Develop reliable automation that reduces manual operational work and improves the consistency and scalability of infrastructure management</li> <li>Build tools and interfaces that enable engineers and other systems to interact programmatically with physical infrastructure</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Provisioning & Lifecycle Management</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Build and extend systems for server discovery, provisioning, configuration, validation, and lifecycle management</li> <li>Automate infrastructure bring-up and capacity deployment across large fleets of compute systems</li> <li>Integrate software and automation with hardware management and provisioning systems</li> <li>Improve tooling and workflows for managing infrastructure throughout its production lifecycle</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Reliability & Observability</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Build telemetry, logging, and observability capabilities that provide visibility into the health of our infrastructure</li> <li>Develop tools and automation to identify, diagnose, and respond to infrastructure and hardware issues</li> <li>Translate recurring operational issues and hardware failure modes into improvements to software, tooling, and automation</li> <li>Improve the reliability and scalability of infrastructure operations as the fleet grows</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Architecture & Collaboration</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Partner with Network, Infrastructure Operations, Data Center, Platform Engineering, and other teams to define requirements and build new infrastructure capabilities</li> <li>Participate in architectural discussions and help define the technical direction of Lightning AI’s infrastructure software</li> <li>Make pragmatic design decisions that balance reliability, scalability, simplicity, and speed of execution</li> <li>Write clear design documents and technical documentation and contribute to engineering best practices</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Who You Are</strong></h2> <h3><strong>Required Qualifications</strong></h3> <ul> <li>5+ years of professional software engineering, infrastructure engineering, or related experience</li> <li>Strong software engineering fundamentals and experience building production backend systems in Python or similar object-oriented programming languages</li> <li>Strong experience with Linux in production environments</li> <li>Experience building APIs, tooling, or automation for managing infrastructure at scale</li> <li>Familiarity with containerization and orchestration concepts</li> <li>Understanding of HPC and bare-metal infrastructure fundamentals, including provisioning and out-of-band management</li> <li>Ability to navigate ambiguity and make pragmatic architecture decisions while building for long-term reliability and scale</li> <li>Experience working in a startup or other fast-paced environment with a high degree of ownership and autonomy</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Ideal Experience</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Experience with bare-metal hardware troubleshooting and provisioning, including technologies such as PXE/iPXE, BMC, Redfish, or particularly SONiC switches, Palo Alto firewalls, or Juniper Networks</li> <li>Experience with high-performance storage systems, particularly VAST</li> <li>Experience supporting AI/ML or HPC infrastructure at scale</li> </ul> <h2> </h2> <h2>Compensation</h2><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p>We are committed to offering competitive title: VP, Strategic Finance
description: Team: Finance (G&A) Reports to: Chief Financial Officer Location: London, Amsterdam or Stockholm. Remote-first, with travel as and when needed About Nivoda Nivoda is the B2B marketplace rebuilding how the jewellery industry works. We connect independent jewellery retailers with a global network of diamond and gemstone suppliers, so a jeweller in Denver or Devon can source from anywhere in the world without the cost, risk, and hassle of doing it the old way. We handle the logistics, the payments, and the quality checks, the messy middle that used to put global sourcing out of reach for small businesses. Today we process over $300M in transactions a year in a $350B industry that still runs largely on personal relationships and paperwork. We are growing quickly, we are backed by leading investors, and we are only getting started. We built Nivoda so every jeweller, whatever their size and wherever they are, has access to the same global supply, pricing and tools as the biggest players. Why this role & why now You will sit on the Extended Leadership Team, report to the CFO, and own how Nivoda plans, reports and is funded. You will present to the board, investors and our receivables lender yourself, work directly with the CFO on equity and debt financing, and build a finance function that runs on routine rather than heroics. This is for someone who wants to lead a team and shape the company’s financial story, not only model it. What you will own Planning and forecasting. You own the annual budget, quarterly reforecast and long-range plan, plus scenario and funding cases for the C-suite and board. You are accountable for forecast accuracy against agreed tolerances, and for an honest post-mortem whether we miss or overachieve. Board, investor and lender reporting. You own the monthly board pack and the numbers behind it, plus materials for existing and prospective investors and our receivables lender, including covenant reporting and onsite diligence. You present to these audiences yourself and you are their first call for analytical questions. The aim is that they trust the numbers without the CFO needing to vouch for them. Corporate finance. You build the models and documentation for equity and debt financing, analyse term sheets, work with the People team on cap table and option pool, and support the CFO on transactions. Commercial and unit economics. You own cohort economics, customer lifetime value, geographic and segment profitability, and the return on marketing and sales spend. With the CRO’s organisation, you build quota and commission models so targets, incentives and the forecast point at the same numbers. Business partnering. You partner with Product and Engineering, Fulfilment, Fintech and the commercial teams on build versus buy, hiring cases, pricing and fee experiments, and capital allocation. The function says yes, no or not yet, with a model behind it. Leading the function. You lead the team: hiring, onboarding, objectives, development and performance, including written objectives and regular structured feedback for each person. You set the review standard and deliverables calendar, agree data contracts with the Data team, and own the tooling (Snowflake, NetSuite, ThoughtSpot, Claude and the modelling stack). We measure the function on on-time delivery, errors caught internally rather than by the audience, forecast accuracy, and how many people can produce each recurring deliverable. What good looks like First 90 days. You have taken over the monthly pack and the reforecast without the investors noticing a handover. You have met your leadership-team peers and told the CFO what you would change and in what order. 90 to 180 days. The monthly pack, FP&A-approved numbers and lender reporting land on the agreed date, each with a named owner and a written process. No board, lender or investor number has needed restating. The first version of the business line P&Ls is delivered at day 180. Twelve months. The function delivers month-end and board commitments without you or the CFO stepping in, including when you are away. A team member has delivered a new analytical capability end to end. FP&A and the Data team work from one set of metric definitions. Board members, lenders and the leadership team rely on the numbers without asking the CFO to vouch for them. The standard A finance team has no quota. The thing it sells is trust, and trust is earned with accuracy a bar above the rest of the company and delivery on the date promised. Three things must not fail in this role. Timeliness : deadlines are commitments, not targets. Quality : every external-facing number reconciles to a primary source and has been reviewed by someone other than its author before it leaves the team. Capacity : within reason, not a constraint. The function absorbs the demands of a 450-person company by organising, prioritising and delegating. If capacity is a hard limit, you make the case for a hire or an automation with numbers, rather than letting the work slip. That is a high bar, and it is fair because the role comes with the means to meet it: people to delegate to, authority over how the team's week is spent, a budget line, and the standing to say no to the business with the CFO's backing. What you bring A background in investment banking, FP&A or venture capital, building models that senior stakeholders made decisions on. You have led a team, directly or through managers, and you want the management part of this role. You have presented to boards, investors or lenders as the person answering the question, not the person who built the slide. A working understanding of marketplace dynamics: two-sided liquidity, take rates, usage-based revenue without a contract, and what FX does to all of it. Complex cohort modelling is native to you. You are comfortable in Snowflake and a modern BI tool, you treat AI tooling as part of the stack, and you would rather fix the pipeline than reformat the output every month. You are calm under pressure, low on ego and allergic to spin. You tell people the uncomfortable thing early. Useful but not required: receivables financing or lender reporting, a multi-jurisdiction group, NetSuite, or a business that trades physical goods across borders. What this role is not It is not a bigger version of a senior analyst role, and it is not where every difficult model gets built personally. If you are at your best as the smartest modeler in the room and would rather stay that way, this will frustrate you. It is also not a quiet seat. Month-end, board and lender deadlines are fixed, a 450-person company makes a lot of demands on finance, and you will regularly be the one saying no, with the CFO’s backing. If you want a purely advisory or slower-paced role, this isn’t it. What we offer Nivoda is a place where smart, driven people do the best work of their careers. We move fast, give ownership early, and don’t have layers of bureaucracy slowing things down. If you see a problem, you can fix it. Our current benefits include: Flexible working hours and a vibrant, remote-first company culture Unlimited holiday allowance Participation in our equity programme Genuine opportunities for growth: we promote from within and invest in your development The chance to join during an expansion phase and shape how Nivoda operates at scale Interview Process Screening conversation with Talent Acquisition Structured career-history interview with Hiring Manager Focus interview: you present a case study to a panel from Finance and the leadership team Final conversation with the C-suite Equal opportunity Nivoda is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. If you meet most of this description and not all of it, apply anyway and tell us where the gaps are. Please submit your CV in English. Not the right role? Join our Talent Pool If this isn’t quite the right fit but you’re excited about what Nivoda is building, we’d still love to hear from you. Join our Talent Pool and we’ll reach out when the right opportunity comes along. nivoda.com/careers Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Patent Engineer (Life Sciences)
description: The way companies innovate is broken. The systems built to create and protect ideas can’t keep up with the pace of change. Today, 90% of S&P 500 company value is intangible (e.g., in intellectual property) - yet R&D and IP teams spend half their time buried in manual work , sifting through patents and paperwork instead of pushing the frontier forward. The tools of creating and protecting are stuck in the past. We’re here to fix that. Ankar is building the R&D tools for the AI era and defining what applied research will look like in the next 20 years . We’re building infrastructure and product experiences our customers rely on every day. You’ll translate messy, ambiguous problems into clean, dependable software—and you’ll do it at the cutting-edge of AI. We’re at an inflection point: We’ve raised >$24M to date from Tier-1 VCs like Atomico, Index Ventures, Norrsken, Daphni, and angels like the Founder of Hugging Face, CEO from Datadog, and Leaders from DeepMind and OpenAI. We’re already working with the world’s most innovative companies including Fortune 500 company L’Oréal and global law firm Vorys Expanding our world-class team with alumni from Palantir, Amazon, and BCG to tackle the $1T+ innovation market . We’re just getting started. What you’ll be doing We’re looking for a patent professional with deep large-molecule life sciences expertise who can bridge product development, engineering and IP protection. You’ll work hands-on with pharmaceutical and biotech customers to design AI-powered patent solutions that understand the nuances of biologics—including antibodies, proteins, peptides, nucleic acids, vaccines and cell and gene therapies—and the conventions that govern their patent protection. Build life sciences-specific patent products: Partner with product and engineering teams to develop AI tools tailored to large-molecule patents—from protein and antibody sequence analysis to biologics claim generation, sequence-listing support and prior-art searching across life sciences databases. Embed with pharmaceutical and biotech customers: Work directly with in-house patent counsel and prosecution teams to design, prototype and deploy high-value proofs of concept for large-molecule patent workflows. Shape product development with biologics expertise: Translate complex large-molecule patent challenges into product requirements, ensuring our AI understands sequence data, CDR and epitope definitions, functional claim language, sequence variants, experimental data and biologics drafting conventions. Drive customer success in large-molecule patents: Lead technical sessions with patent professionals to ensure our products deliver measurable value across biologics patent portfolios. Identify emerging biologics patent opportunities: Recognize evolving needs across therapeutic antibodies, recombinant proteins, vaccines, nucleic acid technologies, cell and gene therapies, biologics formulations and regulatory IP strategy. What we’re looking for Large-molecule patent expertise: At least two years of experience in biologics patent prosecution, pharmaceutical or biotech IP, or other large-molecule-focused patent work, with a strong understanding of the patent lifecycle from invention disclosure through prosecution, grant and enforcement. Technical life sciences foundation: Strong knowledge of molecular biology, biochemistry, immunology or a related discipline, including an understanding of protein and nucleic acid sequences, antibody structure and function, biologics development, and how these translate into patentable subject matter. Strong biologics drafting skills: Experience developing claim strategies for antibodies, proteins, nucleic acids or other biologic modalities, with an understanding of written-description, enablement, sequence-listing and functional-claiming requirements. Builder’s mindset: You thrive in ambiguity, iterate quickly on prototypes and enjoy creating order from complexity. You can move seamlessly between high-level patent strategy and detailed biologics claim construction. Extreme ownership: You anticipate problems, take responsibility for outcomes and consistently deliver. This is how you grow—and how we win. [Bonus points]: Experience at a patent law firm representing pharmaceutical or biotech clients; in-house patent counsel experience at a pharmaceutical or biotech company; expertise in emerging modalities such as antibody-drug conjugates, bispecific antibodies, RNA therapeutics or cell and gene therapies; or an advanced life sciences degree combined with patent training. This role is not for you if... You need a highly structured environment, a predefined playbook, regular working hours, or a schedule that never requires travel. We operate with high autonomy and ownership, expect our team to go above and beyond, be obsessed with our mission and thrive in ambiguity rather than wait for direction. You prefer long planning cycles and certainty before acting. We move quickly, ship often, and adapt based on customer feedback and new information. You want to manage the work rather than do the work. We're builders first, and everyone is expected to contribute directly to creating exceptional products. You take it personally when ideas are challenged, priorities shift, or work gets redirected. We care more about finding the right answer than defending a particular one. What we put behind our people Building at the frontier takes exceptional people. We invest accordingly. Health Insurance : Full private health & dental coverage for you and your dependents. Pension: Flexible pension scheme with up to 5% employer matching on qualifying earnings. Food on us: Team lunches twice a week, plus dinner when working late in the office. Cycle to work: Green Commute initiative scheme (up to £3k) to help you get a new bike tax-free. Way we work: We combine deep, in-person collaboration (3 days/week in our Shoreditch office) with flexibility and trust. What matters is ownership, impact, and results, not where you work from. Strong commercial judgement in prioritizing prospects, shaping warm introductions, and managing opportunities with sales teams. Experience executing partner go-to-market activity, such as enablement, account mapping, campaigns, events, or co-sell programs. Comfort using performance data to assess partner activity, report results, and adjust course. Excellent written, verbal, and listening skills, with the ability to work across partner organizations and internal teams. A hands-on, organized working style that keeps multiple relationships and commitments moving at once. UK-based, with flexibility to travel across the UK and attend occasional evening or weekend partner events. Nice to haves A background in strategy consulting or investment banking. Experience creating B2B pipeline through partner networks, executive events, hospitality, or account-based campaigns. Familiarity with UK small and medium-sized businesses and the finance leaders who buy and use Ramp's products. Experience building a new partner motion in a growing market or adapting a successful approach to a new partner category.
